### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, touching **16** documentable anchor(s).

**20** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c4cb5ec0c3936dd2c24ae2aa9a349449d8e33bef`.

⛔ **7** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **58** of **210** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c4cb5ec0c3936dd2c24ae2aa9a349449d8e33bef` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `deb0226e20bbe36cc1467b064faa2b125befa656` — the merge of head `fd02314b73a44b821cc9a3ccbf27f43114e3ac56` into base `c4cb5ec0c3936dd2c24ae2aa9a349449d8e33bef`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin deb0226e20bbe36cc1467b064faa2b125befa656 && git checkout deb0226e20bbe36cc1467b064faa2b125befa656
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin c4cb5ec0c3936dd2c24ae2aa9a349449d8e33bef fd02314b73a44b821cc9a3ccbf27f43114e3ac56 && git checkout -B drift-repro c4cb5ec0c3936dd2c24ae2aa9a349449d8e33bef && git merge --no-ff fd02314b73a44b821cc9a3ccbf27f43114e3ac56

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c4cb5ec0c3936dd2c24ae2aa9a349449d8e33bef
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs c4cb5ec0c3936dd2c24ae2aa9a349449d8e33bef` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `fd02314b73a44b821cc9a3ccbf27f43114e3ac56`
Local-runs: probe — a node one-liner comparing the save-door message literal on `main` (7b8bcfe2) with the one the head builds with no `door`, to answer the byte-identity question (equal); nothing of the tree was built, run or re-run (`record-recognisers.mjs --template` was printed for the record's shape only)
Scope: packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-authoring-gate.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-datasource-credentials-ref.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.datasource-credentials-ref-restore-doors.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/datasource-credentials-ref-restore-doors.dogfood.test.ts, scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json + packages/metadata-protocol/src/sys-metadata-repository.ts (`restoreVersion`, `promoteDraft`, `headAt`, `resolveWriteHead`, `whereFor`), packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-stored-row-bindings.ts (`resolveOverlayPackageBinding`), PR #27817's record (comment 6512185647: the judge's address, order and pass-through, reused where unchanged). The changeset `.changeset/27818-datasource-restore-publish-credentials-ref.md` is a prose face: the lane seat's ACCEPT.

### ① Derived judgments

- **The rule.** #27582's, as #27817 applied it at the metadata save door: a non-system write may only seal a new value or keep its own record's stored reference. The doors that make a stored body the active `datasource` row seal nothing, so each has an accept set of one value for `external.credentialsRef`: the one the active row it writes into holds now. Extending the same judge to those doors is the rule, not a new one.
- **Accept set, before → after**, per door:
  - `rollbackMetaItem` (REST `POST /api/v1/meta/datasource/:name/rollback`) and `revertCommit`'s restore limb (`POST /api/v1/packages/:id/commits/:commitId/revert`, and through it `rollbackToPackageCommit`): before, a history version was written back with whatever reference it stored; now a version naming a reference the active row does not hold now is refused `VALIDATION_ERROR` / 400. **Correct.**
  - `promoteDraftForPublish` (the per-item `POST /api/v1/meta/datasource/:name/publish` and the package publish batch, both reach it): before, a draft went live with whatever reference it stored; now a draft naming a reference the active row at `promoteInto` does not hold is refused the same way, before `repo.promoteDraft`. **Correct.**
  - Still accepted at every door: a body naming the reference its row holds now (kept); a body naming none (stored with none, as a save omitting the key is — the same reading #27817 accepted). Both pinned at each door.
- **Q1 — the save door's words are byte-identical** to #27817's: the head's three-way message builds the no-`door` string from the same fragments, and the two literals compare equal (the probe above). `door` changes only the words: the judged address, the comparison and the pass-through are the lines #27817 reviewed, unchanged. **One answer per door whatever the reference names:** each door's message names the datasource and the key only; the unit pin asserts the four refusal answers at each door are equal and that none contains any reference; the dogfood pin asserts code and status at the REST doors as a signed-in non-system caller. Holds.
- **Q2 — each call reads the row its write lands in.**
  - Restore: `restoredBodyWriter` is handed `binding` = `resolveOverlayPackageBinding(type, name, member)`, the `package_id` of the active row found by the package-agnostic `(type, name, state: 'active', member)` lookup; `restoreVersion` runs `deriveRestoredBody` first, then finds the active row with the same package-agnostic lookup and `put`s with that row's `package_id`. The judge reads `headAt(active, packageId: binding, member)`, an exact `package_id` match (string → eq, `null` → IS NULL), which is the address the `put` resolves to (`resolveWriteHead` with `state: 'active'` does no fallback). Same row.
  - Publish: `promoteDraft` writes the active row at `draftRow.package_id ?? adoptInto ?? null`; with `packageId: draftKey` and `adoptInto: promoteInto` (only when `draftKey === null`), that is `promoteInto` in every branch. The judge reads `headAt(active, packageId: promoteInto)`. Same row, and the same key the other publish-side save-door judges in that block already read.
  - `source: undefined` at both call sites, so neither takes the server-stated pass-through; no restore or publish caller states a source (read tree-wide: `repo.restoreVersion` and `repo.promoteDraft` have exactly the three callers in `protocol.ts`).
- **Q3 — placement and coverage.** The restore judge sits in `refuseRestoredBodyTheSaveDoorRefuses`, after `unknownDatasourceSaveRefusal` and before the elevated-flow and runtime-authoring checks, in the save door's order; it runs inside `restoreVersion` before the active row is read and before the `put`. The publish judge sits after `unknownDatasourceSaveRefusal` and before `repo.promoteDraft`. Nothing is written on either path before the refusal (the unit pin snapshots the store before and after each refusal, equal; the dogfood pin reads the active row back unchanged). Every path that turns a stored body into the active datasource row from the protocol is judged: `rollbackMetaItem`, `revertCommit`'s restore limb, `rollbackToPackageCommit` (runs `revertCommit` per commit), the per-item publish and `publishPackageDrafts` (both through `promoteDraftForPublish`). The remaining stored-row writer is `migrateStoredMetadata` (`source: 'migrate-stored'`), the server-stated rewrite of a row's own body that #27817 accepted as the pass-through; a package install writes from a manifest, not a stored body, and the package duplicate and unmanaged import go through `saveMetaItem`, judged since #27817. No reactivation door exists.
- **Package publish batch:** one `promoteDraftForPublish` throw is re-thrown with `__batchItem` out of the loop, inside `inTxn`; with an engine `transaction()` the batch rolls back whole. That is how every per-item refusal in the batch already behaves; nothing is changed here.
- **Published surface:** no export, type or schema moves; `datasourceCredentialsRefSaveRefusal` is unexported and gains an optional parameter. `DatasourceSchema` untouched.
- **Q5 — the ledger.** The new unit pin's stub binds `delete`, `findOne` and `update` to the engine-double predicates: three rows, one per bound verb (15 lines), none lost; `Lint · ESLint`, which carries the `Engine test-double contract gate`, is green at the head.

### ② Semver level

- `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`: **`minor`**, with `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` line-initial on the PR body and the changeset, the BREAKING banner, the `!` title and one ADR-0087 marker. `narrowed` is the kind (three doors refuse a value they wrote before); a kind other than `none` takes at least `minor` (AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3). Consistent, and the same level and kind as #27817.
- ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`: no key, export or type is added, removed or re-shaped; the changeset carries a remedy for the request (restore a version naming the served reference, re-save with the key omitted, bind through the admin door), not a prescription for rewriting stored data. `Check Changeset` is green at the head. Correct.
- `Skills-docs: none — REASON` present on the PR body (lane seat's ACCEPT to confirm the sentence).

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Q4 — the two stated side effects are acceptable.** A rollback or revert to a version whose reference the row no longer holds (rotated since, or stored before the save door judged the key), and a publish of a draft stored before a rotation, are now refused. Both are the rule's own consequence (a reference an active row does not hold now is not that row's to carry forward), both are stated in the changeset under *Who sees it*, and each carries a remedy that keeps the capability reachable through the door that mints a reference. No silent loss: the refusal names the door.
- **Package rollback reporting (pre-existing, stated in the PR).** `rollbackToPackageCommit` counts a commit as reverted when `revertCommit` does not throw; a per-item refusal, this one included, lands in the inner `failed[]`, which the package rollback does not surface. The shape is every per-item refusal's on that path and is not changed here. The seat may file a report-only follow-up (surface the inner `failed[]`), outside this card.
- **Batch publish on an engine without `transaction()`** (the memory driver): items promoted before a refused one stay promoted. Pre-existing for every refusal in the batch; not this diff's.
- **Q6 — `Fixes #27818`.** Item 1 (restore doors) is measured, pinned and fixed at this head. Item 2 asked for a decision on whether rows stored before the rule need an audit; comment 6512713420 on the card answers it at rule level: what `os secret orphans` covers, four readings it misses, what an operator can do today, and a report-only tooling change proposed outside the card's surface; no migration or repair is proposed. That is the decision the item asked for, so `Fixes` is acceptable. The card's trailing point *for the maintainer to decide* (whether a definition read should keep serving the reference to every reader) is not answered by this PR or the comment; it is a maintainer decision, not a seat's. The lane seat should carry it (a follow-up card, or the maintainer's word on the card) before or at close, so the close does not drop it.
- **Dogfood battery at fd02314b:** 4 reds, all in files this diff does not touch (`error-sentences-live` ×2, `object-hook-lifecycle-scratch` ×1 — the hook-abort answer, #27806; `platform-app-object-entry-views` ×1 — main-side). The PR body shows the same four red with this change's runtime code absent. Consistent with the tree; none from this diff.
- **Check-runs at this head:** no red; the `Test Core` shards, `Build Core`, `Type Check · workspace/consumer gates/debt ledger` and several `Lint · scoped` jobs were still in progress when read. Landing waits for all green.
- Author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no outside-author note owed.

### ④ Design judgment

- **`protocol-datasource-credentials-ref.ts`:** the right shape — one judge, one address read, one comparison; the new parameter changes words only, so the three doors cannot drift from the save door's rule. The restore and publish words say what each door may bring back and name the remedy. Holds against the cited code and #27582's shape.
- **`protocol-authoring-gate.ts`:** the call sits in the save-door refusal family the restore doors already ask, with the one host member it needs (`getOverlayRepo`) added to the `Pick`; it is asked as an active write against the binding the restore writes under. Holds.
- **`protocol.ts`:** one host line, one docblock bullet and one call-site block beside the other save-door judges the promotion re-asks, on the same `promoteInto` key; nothing moves (serial queue #25467). Holds.
- **Against the published spec on `main`:** `DatasourceSchema` keeps `external.credentialsRef` authorable and documents that the door that binds a secret writes it. This narrowing makes that invariant real at the three doors that could otherwise revive a stored value the row no longer holds; no declared capability is taken from a consumer (the Console saves through the admin door; no SDK method sets the key).
- **Tests:** the unit pin drives the real `rollbackMetaItem`, `revertCommit` and `publishMetaItem` over a stub held to the engine-double predicates, asserts code and status, a byte-identical store and the row's reference kept on every refusal, equal answers across the four refusal cases per door, no reference in any message, `revertCommit`'s `failed[]` entry, and both acceptances per door; the dogfood pin holds the rule at the booted REST doors as a non-system caller. The ablation readings in the PR body match the pin's shape.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-rkqt9u`
Reviewed-by: `session_016WV4czuTWNgKR22fKv7jia (seat subagent)`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## Seat ACCEPT · PR #27860 · head `fd02314b73a44b821cc9a3ccbf27f43114e3ac56` · 2026-10-30T02:39Z

## 维护者速读

The #27582 own-reference rule that #27817 set at the metadata save door now also holds at the doors that turn a stored body into the active `datasource` row: rollback, a commit revert's restore, and a draft publish (including a package publish). Each one refuses a body whose `external.credentialsRef` is not the reference its row holds now. The refusal is `400 VALIDATION_ERROR`, gives one answer whatever the body names, and comes before anything is written. There are two visible side effects, both stated with their remedy in the changeset: a rollback to a version from before a credential rotation is refused, and so is a draft publish after one. Item 2 (rows stored before the fix) is answered as a read-only audit on the card (6512713420). Item 3 is the maintainer's and moves to #27884.

## 席位核对

- **Shape:** draft → main, with `Fixes #27818`. The judge in `protocol-datasource-credentials-ref.ts` gains a door word; the save-door message is byte-identical to #27817's. There is one call in `protocol-authoring-gate.ts` (restore) and one block in `protocol.ts` `promoteDraftForPublish` (publish), with nothing moved in the #25467 hot file. Also a unit pin, a dogfood pin, and `scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json` (gate-derived). `check-governed-merges --pr 27860`: NOT governed, +664 / −8.
- **Contract review:** `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` record 6513450055, **PASS** at this head (claim 6513366341).
- **Declarations:** `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` minor, `!` title, BREAKING banner, ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`. Consistent.
- **Skills-docs:** `none`, with the reason on the PR body. The seat confirms no `skills/**` page teaches restoring or publishing a datasource with a hand-written reference.
- **Dogfood battery** (owed by the `!` title): 4 red tests, all main-side and red on the base build too: 3 under #27806 and 1 under #27813 (red 2). This PR's own pins are green.
- **Item 3 of #27818** (whether a definition read serves the reference) is the maintainer's, so it is split to #27884 before this PR closes the card.
- **Out of scope, filed:** #27868 (a package rollback drops per-item refusals).
- **Gate check-runs on this head:** 49 total, 36 success, 13 skipped by the path filter, 0 failed. `mergeable_state: clean`.
- **Landing:** Tier S, under the maintainer's landing grant for this term (2026-10-29 22:05Z, seat thread). Ready + auto-merge through the relay.
